title: The Sixth Extinction: An Unnatural History
author: Elizabeth Kolbert

review_summary_highlights: Praised for making mass extinction urgent and readable.
Readers value the field reporting across continents.

one_sentence_hook: We are living through a sixth mass extinction, and human activity is the asteroid.

summary.overview: Elizabeth Kolbert travels the world to document how human activity is driving species to extinction at unprecedented rates, weaving field reporting with deep time history.
key_takeaways: Current extinction rates far exceed background rates.

title: The Gene: An Intimate History
author: Siddhartha Mukherjee

review_summary_highlights: Praised for weaving science with family narrative.
Readers value the ethical questions raised.

one_sentence_hook: The story of the gene is the story of how we came to read, and rewrite, ourselves.

summary.overview: Siddhartha Mukherjee traces the history of genetics from Mendel to CRISPR, blending science, history, and personal family stories.
key_takeaways: Genes are not destiny; environment and chance matter.
Genetic knowledge carries profound ethical weight.
The line between therapy and enhancement blurs.

title: A Short History of Nearly Everything
author: Bill Bryson

review_summary_highlights: Praised for making science accessible and entertaining.
Readers love Bryson's curiosity and humor.

one_sentence_hook: A witty tour of everything science knows about the universe and our place in it.

summary.overview: Bill Bryson explains the history of the universe, Earth, and life in accessible prose, celebrating the scientists behind discoveries.
key_takeaways: Science is a human endeavor full of accidents and personalities.
The universe is vast and our knowledge is hard-won.

title: Astrophysics for People in a Hurry
author: Neil deGrasse Tyson

review_summary_highlights: Praised for its concise cosmic overview.
Readers value the accessible tone.

one_sentence_hook: The universe in your pocket: key cosmic ideas explained in bite-sized chapters.

summary.overview: Neil deGrasse Tyson distills the essentials of astrophysics into short, readable chapters for busy readers.
key_takeaways: The universe is knowable through observation.

title: The Body: A Guide for Occupants
author: Bill Bryson

review_summary_highlights: Praised for its awe at human biology.
Readers value the surprising facts.

one_sentence_hook: Your body is the most complex machine you will ever inhabit, and it is largely a mystery to you.

summary.overview: Bill Bryson explores the human body system by system, celebrating its complexity and the science that studies it.
key_takeaways: Small habits compound into health outcomes.

title: Predictably Irrational
author: Dan Ariely

review_summary_highlights: Praised for revealing hidden forces behind decisions.
Readers enjoy the experiments.

one_sentence_hook: Your decisions are less rational than you think, and the patterns are predictable.

summary.overview: Dan Ariely uses behavioral experiments to show how irrationality shapes pricing, choices, and social norms.
key_takeaways: Free is a powerful and distorting price.
Social and market norms should not mix.

title: The Paradox of Choice: Why More Is Less
author: Barry Schwartz

review_summary_highlights: Praised for articulating choice overload.
Readers value the satisficer vs maximizer distinction.

one_sentence_hook: More choice can make us less happy and less able to choose.

summary.overview: Barry Schwartz argues that an abundance of options increases anxiety and regret, proposing satisficing as an antidote.
key_takeaways: Maximizers suffer more regret than satisficers.

title: Stumbling on Happiness
author: Daniel Gilbert

review_summary_highlights: Praised for its wit and research synthesis.
Readers value the imagination pitfalls.

one_sentence_hook: We are terrible at predicting what will make us happy, and science explains why.

summary.overview: Daniel Gilbert examines why humans mispredict their future happiness and how memory and imagination distort foresight.
key_takeaways: Happiness is partly constructed in the present.

title: The Happiness Hypothesis
author: Jonathan Haidt

review_summary_highlights: Praised for blending ancient wisdom with modern research.
Readers value the rider and elephant metaphor.

one_sentence_hook: Ancient wisdom and modern psychology converge on how to live a meaningful life.

summary.overview: Jonathan Haidt explores ten great ideas from ancient traditions through the lens of contemporary psychology.
key_takeaways: The mind is divided like a rider and an elephant.
Happiness comes from between, not within.

title: Flow: The Psychology of Optimal Experience
author: Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi

review_summary_highlights: Praised for defining peak experience precisely.
Readers value the challenge-skill balance.

one_sentence_hook: Happiness is not pleasure but deep absorption in challenging, meaningful activity.

summary.overview: Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi describes flow, the state of complete immersion, and how to cultivate it in work and life.
key_takeaways: Flow arises when challenge matches skill.
Attention is the currency of experience.

title: Mindset: The New Psychology of Success
author: Carol S. Dweck

review_summary_highlights: Praised for the growth vs fixed distinction.
Readers value the parenting and teaching implications.

one_sentence_hook: Believing abilities can grow changes how you face failure and effort.

summary.overview: Carol Dweck contrasts fixed and growth mindsets and shows how beliefs about ability shape achievement and resilience.
key_takeaways: Praise effort and strategy, not innate talent.
Growth mindset can be cultivated at any age.

title: Grit: The Power of Passion and Perseverance
author: Angela Duckworth

review_summary_highlights: Praised for elevating effort over talent.
Readers value the grit scale and stories.

one_sentence_hook: Talent counts, but effort counts twice, and grit is the engine of achievement.

summary.overview: Angela Duckworth argues that passion and perseverance predict success better than talent, drawing on research and stories.
key_takeaways: Effort = talent x effort; achievement = skill x effort.
Purpose and hope sustain long-term grit.

title: Peak: Secrets from the New Science of Expertise
author: Anders Ericsson and Robert Pool

review_summary_highlights: Praised for debunking the 10,000-hour myth's simplicity.
Readers value the deliberate practice breakdown.

one_sentence_hook: Expertise is built, not born, through deliberate practice with feedback.

summary.overview: Anders Ericsson explains the science of expertise, showing how deliberate practice, not innate talent, produces mastery.
key_takeaways: Deliberate practice is purposeful and feedback-driven.
Genetics set ranges, practice determines outcomes.

title: The Hard Thing About Hard Things
author: Ben Horowitz

review_summary_highlights: Praised for candid CEO struggles.
Readers value the wartime CEO framing.

one_sentence_hook: Building a company is brutally hard, and this book is the honest manual no one else writes.

summary.overview: Ben Horowitz shares hard-won lessons on leading through crises, layoffs, and growth as a startup CEO.
key_takeaways: Wartime CEOs differ from peacetime CEOs.
Hiring and firing decisions shape culture.
There are no silver bullets, only lead bullets.

title: Zero to One: Notes on Startups, or How to Build the Future
author: Peter Thiel

review_summary_highlights: Praised for contrarian thinking.
Readers value the monopoly argument.

one_sentence_hook: The best startups create new categories rather than competing in existing ones.

summary.overview: Peter Thiel argues that true progress comes from creating monopolies through unique technology, not incremental competition.
key_takeaways: Competition is for losers; seek monopoly.
Distribution matters as much as product.

title: The Lean Startup
author: Eric Ries

review_summary_highlights: Praised for the build-measure-learn loop.
Readers value MVP thinking.

one_sentence_hook: Startups are experiments, and learning fast beats executing a perfect plan.

summary.overview: Eric Ries presents a scientific approach to building startups through validated learning and rapid iteration.
key_takeaways: Pivot or persevere based on data.

title: Good to Great: Why Some Companies Make the Leap and Others Don't
author: Jim Collins

review_summary_highlights: Praised for the hedgehog concept.
Readers value the level 5 leadership idea.

one_sentence_hook: Good is the enemy of great, and the leap requires disciplined people, thought, and action.

summary.overview: Jim Collins studies companies that sustained great performance and identifies shared disciplines behind their success.
key_takeaways: Level 5 leaders blend humility and will.
The hedgehog concept focuses on what you can be best at.

title: The Innovator's Dilemma
author: Clayton M. Christensen

review_summary_highlights: Praised for explaining why great companies fail.
Readers value the disruptive innovation framework.

one_sentence_hook: The very practices that make companies successful can blind them to disruptive threats.

summary.overview: Clayton Christensen shows how disruptive technologies upend established companies that serve their best customers.
key_takeaways: Disruptive innovations start in low-end or new markets.
Create separate units for disruptive bets.

title: Crossing the Chasm
author: Geoffrey A. Moore

review_summary_highlights: Praised for the technology adoption lifecycle.
Readers value the pragmatist gap insight.

one_sentence_hook: The hardest leap in tech is from early adopters to the mainstream market.

summary.overview: Geoffrey Moore explains the gap between early adopters and the mainstream and how to position products to cross it.
key_takeaways: Pragmatists buy complete solutions, not technology.
The whole product concept wins mainstream buyers.

title: Measure What Matters
author: John Doerr

review_summary_highlights: Praised for popularizing OKRs.
Readers value the case studies.

one_sentence_hook: Objectives and key results turn ambition into measurable, aligned execution.

summary.overview: John Doerr explains the OKR framework through stories from Google, Intel, and others.

title: High Output Management
author: Andrew S. Grove

review_summary_highlights: Praised for its practical managerial cadence.
Readers value the leverage concept.

one_sentence_hook: A manager's output is the output of their team, and leverage is how you multiply it.

summary.overview: Andrew Grove distills management into processes, leverage, and meetings that produce high output.
key_takeaways: Meetings are a medium of work, not a waste.

title: The Culture Code: The Secrets of Highly Successful Groups
author: Daniel Coyle

review_summary_highlights: Praised for its vivid group examples.
Readers value the three skills framework.

one_sentence_hook: Great cultures are built through safety, vulnerability, and purpose, not perks.

summary.overview: Daniel Coyle studies high-performing groups to identify the skills that build strong culture.

title: The Warmth of Other Suns
author: Isabel Wilkerson

review_summary_highlights: Praised for its epic narrative of the Great Migration.
Readers value the three protagonists.

one_sentence_hook: The Great Migration reshaped America, told through three unforgettable lives.

summary.overview: Isabel Wilkerson chronicles the decades-long migration of Black Americans from the South through three personal stories.
key_takeaways: The Great Migration was a leaderless revolution.
Migrants carried culture and reshaped cities.

title: Caste: The Origins of Our Discontents
author: Isabel Wilkerson

review_summary_highlights: Praised for reframing American racism as caste.
Readers value the historical parallels.

one_sentence_hook: American inequality is better understood as a caste system than as individual prejudice.

summary.overview: Isabel Wilkerson compares the American caste system to those of India and Nazi Germany to illuminate structural hierarchy.
key_takeaways: Awareness is the first step to dismantling it.

title: 1491: New Revelations of the Americas Before Columbus
author: Charles C. Mann

review_summary_highlights: Praised for overturning myths of empty Americas.
Readers value the indigenous civilizations.

one_sentence_hook: The Americas before Columbus were more populous, cultivated, and sophisticated than we were taught.

summary.overview: Charles Mann synthesizes new research showing dense, engineered, and complex indigenous societies before 1492.

title: Salt: A World History
author: Mark Kurlansky

review_summary_highlights: Praised for making a commodity fascinating.
Readers value the historical breadth.

one_sentence_hook: Salt shaped wars, empires, and economies, and its story is the story of civilization.

summary.overview: Mark Kurlansky follows salt through history, showing how this everyday mineral drove trade, taxation, and conflict.
key_takeaways: Control of salt meant control of power.

title: Cod: A Biography of the Fish That Changed the World
author: Mark Kurlansky

review_summary_highlights: Praised for tracing cod's global impact.
Readers value the ecological warning.

one_sentence_hook: A single fish species shaped empires and is now collapsing under human demand.

summary.overview: Mark Kurlansky tells the history of cod fishing and its role in exploration, trade, and ecological decline.

title: Dead Wake: The Last Crossing of the Lusitania
author: Erik Larson

review_summary_highlights: Praised for its suspenseful narrative.
Readers value the dual perspective.

one_sentence_hook: The sinking of the Lusitania, told with the tension of a thriller.

summary.overview: Erik Larson reconstructs the final voyage of the Lusitania and the U-boat that sank it.
key_takeaways: Intelligence and miscommunication shaped the disaster.
The sinking pushed America toward war.

title: The Splendid and the Vile
author: Erik Larson

review_summary_highlights: Praised for its intimate portrait of Churchill.
Readers value the family dynamics.

one_sentence_hook: Churchill's first year as prime minister, when Britain stood alone against Hitler.

summary.overview: Erik Larson focuses on Churchill's leadership during the Blitz, blending political drama with family life.
key_takeaways: Alliances are built through personal diplomacy.

title: Steve Jobs
author: Walter Isaacson

review_summary_highlights: Praised for its candid portrait of a complex visionary.
Readers value the product philosophy.

one_sentence_hook: The life of the man who put a dent in the universe.

summary.overview: Walter Isaacson's authorized biography traces Steve Jobs's life, leadership, and obsession with design.
key_takeaways: Reality distortion can inspire and harm.
Great products sit at the intersection of technology and humanities.

title: Einstein: His Life and Universe
author: Walter Isaacson

review_summary_highlights: Praised for humanizing a genius.
Readers value the physics explanations.

one_sentence_hook: The man behind relativity, revealed through his science and his stubborn independence.

summary.overview: Walter Isaacson portrays Einstein's life, from patent clerk to icon, and the science that changed physics.
key_takeaways: Imagination and thought experiments drove discoveries.
Science and politics intertwined in his life.

title: Benjamin Franklin: An American Life
author: Walter Isaacson

review_summary_highlights: Praised for its balanced, lively portrait.
Readers value the civic contributions.

one_sentence_hook: The original self-made American, whose curiosity shaped a nation.

summary.overview: Walter Isaacson chronicles Franklin's life as printer, scientist, diplomat, and founding father.

title: Leonardo da Vinci
author: Walter Isaacson

review_summary_highlights: Praised for illuminating Leonardo's notebooks.
Readers value the cross-disciplinary genius.

one_sentence_hook: The ultimate Renaissance man, whose curiosity knew no disciplinary bounds.

summary.overview: Walter Isaacson explores Leonardo's life through his notebooks, art, and scientific inquiry.
key_takeaways: Curiosity and observation are learnable skills.

title: The Wright Brothers
author: David McCullough

review_summary_highlights: Praised for its focus on character and persistence.
Readers value the detailed engineering.

one_sentence_hook: Two bicycle mechanics who taught the world to fly through patience and precision.

summary.overview: David McCullough tells the story of the Wright brothers' invention of powered flight.

author: David McCullough

review_summary_highlights: Praised for its focus on a single pivotal year.
Readers value Washington's leadership.

one_sentence_hook: The year America almost lost its revolution, saved by Washington's resolve.

summary.overview: David McCullough focuses on 1776, from the siege of Boston to the Battle of Trenton.
key_takeaways: The army was fragile and often near collapse.

title: John Adams
author: David McCullough

review_summary_highlights: Praised for its vivid portrait of Adams.
Readers value the Adams-Jefferson friendship.

one_sentence_hook: The principled, prickly founder who helped birth a republic.

summary.overview: David McCullough's biography of John Adams, from Braintree to the presidency.
key_takeaways: Partnership and rivalry shaped the founding.

title: Alexander Hamilton
author: Ron Chernow

review_summary_highlights: Praised for its definitive scholarship.
Readers value the financial system creation.

one_sentence_hook: The immigrant founder who built America's financial system and died in a duel.

summary.overview: Ron Chernow's biography of Alexander Hamilton, from orphan to treasury secretary.
key_takeaways: Hamilton's financial innovations shaped the nation.
Political rivalry defined the early republic.

title: Washington: A Life
author: Ron Chernow

review_summary_highlights: Praised for revealing Washington's humanity.
Readers value the leadership lessons.

one_sentence_hook: The first president was neither a saint nor a simple soldier, but a complex leader.

summary.overview: Ron Chernow's biography of George Washington, from planter to founding father.

title: Grant
author: Ron Chernow

review_summary_highlights: Praised for rehabilitating Grant's reputation.
Readers value the military narrative.

one_sentence_hook: The underestimated general who won the Civil War and struggled as president.

summary.overview: Ron Chernow's biography of Ulysses S. Grant, from failure to victory to the White House.
key_takeaways: Military genius can coexist with political naivety.

title: The Guns of August
author: Barbara W. Tuchman

review_summary_highlights: Praised for its dramatic opening of WWI.
Readers value the diplomatic failures.

one_sentence_hook: How Europe stumbled into World War I through miscalculation and pride.

summary.overview: Barbara Tuchman reconstructs the first month of World War I and the decisions that escalated it.

Readers value the diplomatic failures.

one_sentence_hook: How Europe stumbled into World War I through miscalculation and pride.
